title: What is the initial information architecture of the application shell?
statement: The first slice must choose which views exist: project overview, stage view, artifact tracker, assertion/evidence view, or some subset. The choice determines what the vertical slice has to render and what it may defer.
notes: The vertical slice as scoped needs a stage view at minimum, because it displays the current stage and one stage document. `app/server.mjs` already renders an assertion/evidence view against the same substrate, so that view has a working reference implementation and is the cheapest to reach parity on — which is an argument about ORDER, not about what the first slice must contain. ⚠️ ANSWERED LAST, AND NOT BY RESEARCH (pm, 2026-08-24). This is principally a PRODUCT decision, not a research question: no source settles which views a planning tool should open with. It is sequenced fifth so it is decided under the constraints the other four establish rather than ahead of them — a deployment mode (QST-0017), a component bound on what a document may execute (QST-0018), a server/client module boundary (QST-0020) and a runtime lifecycle (QST-0021) each remove options from the information architecture before it is chosen. Choosing the IA first would mean designing views against constraints nobody had established, and then rediscovering them.
